cards.text: The Pharisees and some of the scribes who came from Jerusalem gather around Jesus. You know that feeling when the boss stands RIGHT behind your desk and suddenly you forget how to type? I bet the disciples know it too.

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes notice something about how some of Jesus' disciples are eating. What is it?

cards.text: Mark stops to explain the tradition of the elders: the Pharisees and all the Jews don't eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.

cards.question: And when the Pharisees and the Jews come back from the ___, they don't eat unless they wash.
Mark says the Pharisees and the Jews have many other traditions to keep. Besides hands, what else gets washed?

cards.text: Pitchers too, and even couches for dining. Friend, they wash the COUCHES, and I sat in a junk drawer for years without anybody dusting me ONCE.

cards.question: So the Pharisees and scribes question Jesus about His disciples. What do they want to know?

answers.text: Why they skip the elders' tradition
Why they work on the Sabbath
Why they don't fast like others

cards.text: Jesus answers them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites,” and then He quotes the prophet. Oof.

cards.question: In the words Jesus quotes from Isaiah, these people honor God with their lips, and their hearts are close to Him. True or false?

cards.text: Isaiah's words go on: they worship in vain, and they teach the precepts of men as doctrine. People's rules, wearing God's apron.

cards.question: Then Jesus says it plainly to the Pharisees and scribes: they've disregarded the ___ of God to keep the tradition of men.

cards.text: He goes on, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.” Neatly, friend. Like folding a fresh apron.

cards.question: Jesus gives the Pharisees and scribes an example, starting with something Moses said. Which command does He bring up?

answers.text: Honor your father and your mother

cards.question: Jesus also reminds them that Moses said anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death. True or false?

cards.text: But here's their tradition: a man can tell his parents that whatever they would have received from him is Corban, a gift devoted to God. Mom needs help with the bills, and he goes, “Ooh, sorry. That's Corban!”

cards.question: Once a man says his help is Corban, what does the Pharisees' tradition permit him to do for his father or mother?
Jesus tells the Pharisees and scribes that by the tradition they've handed down, they ___ the word of God.
Jesus says Corban is the only matter where the Pharisees and scribes do this. True or false?

cards.text: Once again Jesus calls the crowd to Him. And He says, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:” EVERYBODY. Put the phones down for this one.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd what can't defile a man. What is it?

answers.text: Nothing that enters him from the outside
Nothing he says when he's angry

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd it's the things that come out of a man that defile him. True or false?

cards.text: Later Jesus leaves the crowd and goes into the house, and His disciples ask Him about the parable.
Jesus asks them, “Are you still so dull?” Friend, I spent years in a drawer with worn-down edges, and let me tell you, dull is NOT a fun place to be.

cards.question: Jesus explains it to the disciples: what enters a man from the outside can't defile him. Where does it go?

answers.text: Into his stomach and then out
Into his mind and then his words
Into his blood and then his bones

cards.question: Mark adds a note about what Jesus said: thus all foods are ___.
Jesus tells the disciples that what comes out of a man is what defiles him. Where does it come from?

answers.text: From within the hearts of men

cards.text: Then Jesus starts listing what comes out: evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery.

cards.question: Jesus' list stops at things like theft and murder. Something like envy doesn't make it. True or false?

cards.text: The list keeps going: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness. Thirteen things, friend, and not ONE of them is about hands.

cards.question: Jesus wraps it up for the disciples: all these evils come from ___, and these are what defile a man.

findings.problem: The Pharisees and the scribes show up for the first time, but the card never says who they are. Neither group has appeared earlier in this lesson.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke has the disciples nervous and forgetting how to type, and card 2 then reveals their unwashed hands. Together they suggest the disciples forgot to wash because they were nervous. The text gives no reason for the unwashed hands, and Jesus' answer does not treat it as a slip.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Moses shows up for the first time in the lesson as "something Moses said," with no simple note on who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke is a made-up scenario about a parent: "Mom needs help with the bills."

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "Once again...", "And He says...", "EVERYBODY." and "Put the phones down...". Only the opening card may have up to 3 sentences, and every other story card is limited to 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "the market" is a place and two words long. The right answer "within" and the other wrong answer "outside" are single direction words. "the market" doesn't match the other answers in kind or length.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
